title: solution_intent/enrichment.json — the permanent enrichment record (§3.7, D-A16)
description: NOT a scratch file. It survives past disposition as the audit trail: every finding, its evidence, whether it auto-applied or escalated, the operator's call and their rationale. That is what lets someone at G2 ask 'why does §13 say this now?' and get an answer — and **v1 + this file together reconstruct exactly how v2 came to be**. Undispositioned findings live HERE and nowhere else (D-A16): the Solution Intent contains only resolved content, or v2 would ship with 'TBD, awaiting operator' scattered through it. Status is per finding so the walkthrough is resumable — fifty findings will not be dispositioned in one sitting.

v1_sha256.description: The frozen v1 this enrichment was computed against. Enrichment reads a FROZEN document; if it could drift, 'v1 + enrichment.json reconstruct v2' would stop being true.

counts.description: §18's payload — counts only, never a ledger. The claim-by-claim record is this file.

arm.description: impact = Arm 1 (requirement → code, 'what did we miss?'); claim = Arm 2 (claim → code, 'what did we get wrong?'). D-A8.

kind.description: The finding type, which together with claim PROVENANCE decides authority (D-A6/D-A16).

claim_provenance.description: Where the v1 claim came from. THIS is what decides who may correct it: source-derived → auto-correct; operator/frame → escalate (never overrule a human silently); unsourced → auto-fill (D-A6).

evidence.description: The code that grounds the finding. Referenced by path/symbol — never inlined (map don't copy). Required for an auto-applied contradiction, gap-fill or derived impact: an unreviewable auto-correction is exactly what the provenance rule exists to prevent. NOT required for `unverifiable`, where the ABSENCE of a match is the finding — demanding evidence there would make an honest 'no code anywhere addresses this' unrepresentable.

reasoning.description: Why the code means what the finding says. A semantic match carries its reasoning — this is what makes a wrong match REVIEWABLE rather than silently wrong (D-A19).

business_visible.description: Derived impacts only: is this a technical consequence we document, or a change someone has to decide about? The escalate/auto-write discriminator (D-A9).

action.description: auto_applied = grounded and unambiguous, applied without a human. escalated = ambiguous, scope-moving, or would overrule a human — reaches the walkthrough. `none` = nothing to do (a confirmation).

severity.description: material findings get individual attention at the walkthrough; advisory ones batch (D-A17 'triage, do not enumerate').

section_target.description: Where the resolved finding lands. `dropped` is legitimate and means the finding was WRONG (an Arm 1 search miss) — recorded in decisions.jsonl rather than vanishing.

depends_on_finding.description: Dispositions have ORDERING dependencies (D-A17): confirming a finding was a search miss invalidates findings derived from that gap. The walkthrough is not a flat queue.

status.description: Per-finding so the walkthrough is RESUMABLE — the operator can stop and resume without losing position (D-A17).

superseded_by.description: The upstream finding whose reversal withdrew this one's premise. Superseded findings are KEPT — the trail must still show what was believed and why it stopped being believed (D-A17).

superseded_downstream.description: Finding ids superseded automatically when this finding was rejected (reject withdraws the premise, so dependents supersede at disposition time — code_review.md #4). The audit trail of what one reject took down.
